questions.question: Which of the following occurs due to continuous movement of gas particles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diffusion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diffusion** is defined as the intermixing of particles of two different types of matter on their own. This process occurs due to the **continuous, random movement** of particles.
 
• In the context of **gases**, particles possess high **kinetic energy** and move at very high speeds in all directions. Because there are large **intermolecular spaces** between gas particles, they can easily move into the spaces of other substances.
 
• The **Kinetic Molecular Theory** of matter states that particles of matter are never at rest; they are in constant motion. This motion is most pronounced in **gases** compared to solids and liquids.
 
• The rate of **diffusion** increases with an increase in **temperature** because higher temperatures give particles more **kinetic energy**, making them move faster. ***Hence, statement 3 is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Condensation:**

 
 
• This is the process by which a substance changes from a **gaseous state** to a **liquid state**.
 
• It occurs when a gas is cooled or subjected to increased **pressure**, causing particles to lose energy and come closer together.
 
 
 
• **Melting:**
 
 
• Also known as **fusion**, it is the physical process where a **solid** turns into a **liquid**.
 
• This happens at a specific temperature called the **melting point**, where the heat energy overcomes the **intermolecular forces** holding the solid structure together.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation:**
 
 
• It is a **surface phenomenon** in which a liquid changes into **vapour** at any temperature below its boiling point.
 
• Unlike **diffusion**, which is the movement and mixing of particles, **evaporation** specifically refers to the phase transition from liquid to gas at the surface.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Brownian Motion:** This is the **zig-zag**, random motion of microscopic particles suspended in a fluid (liquid or gas) resulting from their collision with the fast-moving atoms or molecules in the gas or liquid. It was first observed by **Robert Brown** in **1827**.
 
• **Graham's Law of Diffusion:** Formulated by **Thomas Graham** in **1833**, this law states that the rate of **diffusion** or effusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its **molar mass**.
 
• **Applications:** Diffusion is responsible for many everyday occurrences, such as the **aroma of food** reaching us from several meters away, the spreading of **fragrance** from a perfume bottle, and the exchange of **oxygen** and **carbon dioxide** in the lungs.

questions.question: Megaphones, loudhailers, and shehnais are designed to:

options.text: convert sound waves into electrical signals
spread sound waves equally in all directions
focus sound waves in a particular direction
reduce the intensity of sound waves

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**focus sound waves in a particular direction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Megaphones**, **loudhailers**, and musical instruments like **shehnais** are specifically designed to send sound waves in a **particular direction** rather than allowing them to spread equally in all directions.
 
• These devices function based on the principle of **multiple reflection of sound**. They typically feature a **tube** followed by a **conical opening**.
 
• The **conical shape** acts as a reflective surface that directs the sound waves emitted from the source toward the front. As the sound waves hit the inner walls of the cone, they undergo **successive reflections**, which guides the sound energy forward toward the audience.
 
• By preventing the sound from dispersing into the surrounding environment, the **intensity** and **loudness** of the sound are significantly increased in the desired path. *Hence, the statement that they focus sound waves in a particular direction is correct.*
 
• The primary objective of this design is to ensure that the sound reaches a **longer distance** with clarity, making it ideal for public addresses or musical performances in open spaces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shehnai:**

 
 
• The **Shehnai** is a classical musical instrument (a **double-reed oboe**) prevalent in **India**, **Pakistan**, and **Bangladesh**.
 
• It was traditionally played in **royal courts** (as part of the **naubat**) and is now a staple in **North Indian weddings** and **temple ceremonies**.
 
• Legendary musician **Ustad Bismillah Khan** is credited with popularizing the **Shehnai** on the global classical stage and was awarded the **Bharat Ratna** in **2001**.
 
 
 
• **Reflection of Sound:**
 
 
• Like light, sound reflects off **solid** or **liquid** surfaces. It follows the **laws of reflection**, where the **angle of incidence** equals the **angle of reflection**.
 
• Hard surfaces are generally better reflectors of sound, whereas soft surfaces tend to absorb sound waves.
 
 
 
• **Stethoscope:**
 
 
• This is a medical instrument used by **doctors** to listen to sounds produced within the body, such as the **heartbeat** or **lung** sounds.
 
• It also works on the principle of **multiple reflection**, where the sound of the heartbeat travels through the **tube** via reflections to reach the doctor's ears.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Soundboards:** In large **concert halls** or **theaters**, **curved soundboards** are often placed behind the speaker or the stage so that sound, after reflection, spreads **uniformly** across the width of the hall.
 
• **Microphones vs. Megaphones:** It is important to distinguish that **microphones** are designed to **convert sound waves into electrical signals**, whereas **megaphones** are acoustic devices meant to **amplify and direct** existing sound waves through physical reflection.
 
• **Longitudinal Waves:** Sound travels through air as **longitudinal waves**, consisting of **compressions** and **rarefactions**. The ability to direct these waves through mechanical design is crucial in **acoustic engineering**.
 
• **Intensity and Amplitude:** The **loudness** of sound depends on its **amplitude**. By focusing the sound in one direction, the **amplitude** of the wave is maintained at a higher level over a greater distance than if the wave were allowed to expand **spherically**.

questions.question: The average age of 24 students of a class is 46 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 47 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Teacher's age = **Old Average** + (**Total Members** × **Increase in Average**)

Number of people after including the teacher = 24 + 1 = **25**

Increase in average = 47 − 46 = **1 year**

Teacher's age = 46 + (25 × 1) = 46 + 25 = **71 years**

**∴ The correct answer is 71 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Average age** of 24 students = 46 years. When the **teacher** is included, the total **group size** becomes 25 and the **new average** becomes 47 years.

**Formula:** Total Sum = **Average** × **Number of items**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1d4dbe6cb3eca5aa1fdcab10541ec091a00458df36838d305c042731b3e8ed72.png] 

⇒ Total age of 24 students = 24 × 46 = **1104 years**

⇒ Total age including teacher = 25 × 47 = **1175 years**

⇒ **Teacher's age** = Total sum with teacher − Total sum of students

⇒ Teacher's age = 1175 − 1104 = **71 years**

**∴ The correct answer is 71 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Properties

If every observation is increased or decreased by a constant value **'k'**, the **new average** also increases or decreases by **'k'**.

Inclusion/Exclusion Rule

Value of New Member = (New Average × New Quantity) − (Old Average × Old Quantity).

Net Deviation

The sum of **deviations** of all terms from the arithmetic mean is always **0**. This property is used to find missing values quickly.</p

questions.question: In a zoo, there are 32 ducks, 41 sheep, 7 horses and some crows. If the total number of feet is 211 more than the number of heads, find the number of crows.
questions.solution:

Let **C** be the number of **crows**. Total animals = 32 + 41 + 7 + C = 80 + C.

Each animal has at least **2 feet**. Extra feet come from **4-legged animals** (sheep and horses).

Equation: Total feet − Total heads = 211.

80 + C + (2 × 41 + 2 × 7) = 211 ⇒ 80 + C + 96 = 211 ⇒ 176 + C = 211 ⇒ C = 35.

**∴ The correct answer is 35 crows.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7df401b1d5767a432f84a5f9cfbcef520304b00dea9521e9eed5e27016c70958.png]

**Condition:** F − H = 211.

⇒ 176 + x = 211.

⇒ x = 211 − 176 = 35.

**∴ The correct answer is 35 crows.**

**__Additional Information__**

Head and Foot Count Logic

For any animal, **Number of Heads** is always 1. 2-legged animals (birds) contribute 2 feet, while 4-legged animals contribute 4 feet.

The Difference Formula

questions.question: 4 men can complete a piece of work in 8 days while 2 women can do it in 10 days. In how many days can 5 women and 8 men complete it?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = 4 Men × 8 days = 32 Man-days = 2 Women × 10 days = 20 Woman-days.

Efficiency ratio: 32M = 20W ⇒ 8M = 5W.

We need to find the time for 5 women and 8 men: (5W + 8M) ⇒ (8M + 8M) = 16M.

Since 4 men take 8 days, 16 men will take (4 × 8) ÷ 16 = 2 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by 4 **men** = 8 days

Time taken by 2 **women** = 10 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of workers × Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Work = 4M × 8 = 32M

⇒ Total Work = 2W × 10 = 20W

⇒ 32M = 20W

⇒ Efficiency of 1 Man (M) ÷ Efficiency of 1 Woman (W) = 20 ÷ 32 = 5 ÷ 8

⇒ Let efficiency of 1 Man = 5 units/day, and efficiency of 1 Woman = 8 units/day

⇒ Total Work = 32 × 5 = 160 units

⇒ Efficiency of 5 women and 8 men = (5 × 8) + (8 × 5) = 40 + 40 = 80 units/day

⇒ Number of days required = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 160 ÷ 80 = 2 days

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work-Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken when work is constant: E₁ × T₁ = E₂ × T₂.

Pipes & Cisterns and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the direct proportion of the total work done by individual workers or their efficiencies when they work for the same duration.</p

questions.question: What is the value of (1 + tan² theta)/(1 + cot² theta) ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Put θ = 45°

⇒ (1 + tan² 45°) ÷ (1 + cot² 45°)

⇒ (1 + 1²) ÷ (1 + 1²) = 2 ÷ 2 = 1

Check options: tan² 45° = 1² = 1

**∴ The correct answer is tan² θ.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Expression (1 + tan² theta)/(1 + cot² theta) 

**Formula Used:** 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ and 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ

⇒ Expression = sec² θ ÷ cosec² θ

⇒ Expression = (1/cos² θ) ÷ (1/sin² θ)

⇒ Expression = (1/cos² θ) × (sin² θ/1)

⇒ Expression = sin² θ ÷ cos² θ

⇒ Expression = (sin θ / cos θ)²

⇒ Expression = tan² θ

**∴ The correct answer is tan² θ.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 and the relationship tan θ = 1 ÷ cot θ.

Reciprocal Relations

sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ and cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ are essential for simplifying complex trigonometric fractions.</p

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 20% of the total votes were declared invalid. The winning candidate received 40% of the valid votes and secured 1,60,000 more valid votes than the runner-up, who received 32% of the valid votes. Find the total number of valid votes.

Given that 8% of **Valid Votes** = 1,60,000

Total **Valid Votes** (100%) = (1,60,000 ÷ 8) × 100

Total **Valid Votes** = 20,00,000

**∴ The correct answer is 20,00,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Winner** share = 40% of valid votes

**Runner-up** share = 32% of valid votes

**Vote Difference** = 1,60,000

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/809fbe3590623f20b92fd1f9aa6addf1d5ba11d208b91b350b9ba3f90d2d5427.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the total **Valid Votes** be V.

⇒ Votes of Winner = 0.40V

⇒ Votes of Runner-up = 0.32V

⇒ Difference = 0.40V − 0.32V = 1,60,000

⇒ 0.08V = 1,60,000

⇒ V = 1,60,000 ÷ 0.08

⇒ V = 1,60,00,000 ÷ 8

⇒ V = 20,00,000

**∴ The correct answer is 20,00,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Valid vs Invalid Votes

**Total Votes** = Valid Votes + Invalid Votes. Only **Valid Votes** are considered for determining the winning margin.

Percentage Base Change

If asked for **Total Votes Cast**: Total = Valid Votes ÷ (100% − Invalid%). In this case, 20,00,000 ÷ 0.80 = 25,00,000.

Winning Margin Rule

Margin = (Winner% − Runner-up%) × Total Valid Votes. Always ensure the percentages refer to the same base.</p

questions.question: A trader marked his goods 35% above its cost price. He then gave a discount of 15%. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Successive Percentage** formula to find the net change.

Net Profit% = a − b − (a × b) ÷ 100, where a = **Markup%** and b = **Discount%**.

Net Profit% = 35 − 15 − (35 × 15) ÷ 100.

Net Profit% = 20 − 5.25 = 14.75%.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.75%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Markup = 35% above CP, Discount = 15% on MP.
**Formulas:** MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ae4e00d27a6f19d30740d7a3edf69882da1ef430ec7f0ad6343c751d18b2a12.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 35% of 100 = 135.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 135 − 15% of 135 = 135 − 20.25 = 114.75.

⇒ **Profit** = SP − CP = 114.75 − 100 = 14.75.

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (14.75 ÷ 100) × 100 = 14.75%.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.75%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The price fixed by the seller on the label is the **Marked Price**. Discount is always calculated on the MP. SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by x% and then y%, the net change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%. For discounts, use negative values.</p

questions.question: The ratio of the speeds of two trucks is 5 : 4. The time taken by the faster truck to cover a distance of 200 km is 2 hours less than the other. Find the speed of the slower truck.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed Ratio** of trucks = 5 : 4

Since distance is constant, **Time Ratio** = Inverse of Speed Ratio = 4 : 5

Difference in time units = 5 − 4 = 1 unit → 2 hours

Time taken by slower truck (5 units) = 5 × 2 = 10 hours

Speed of slower truck = Total Distance ÷ Time = 200 ÷ 10 = 20 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 20 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec5f269cd152d6fcfae2db9d0e90789e7cda1f87b3e7ef42421df237f30fa82c.png] 

**Given:**

Ratio of speeds = 5 : 4

Distance (D) = 200 km

Time difference = 2 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time | Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the speed of the **faster truck** be 5x and **slower truck** be 4x.

⇒ Time taken by slower truck − Time taken by faster truck = 2

⇒ (200 ÷ 4x) − (200 ÷ 5x) = 2

⇒ (50 ÷ x) − (40 ÷ x) = 2

⇒ 10 ÷ x = 2

⇒ x = 5

⇒ Speed of slower truck = 4 × 5 = 20 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 20 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

When the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). If speed ratio is a:b, the time ratio is b:a.

Average Speed Formula

For the same distance covered at two different speeds u and v, Average Speed = (2 × u × v) ÷ (u + v).

Relative Speed

In the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. In the opposite direction, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: A and B working together can do a piece of work in 3 days. B alone can do the same work in 6 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to do double the work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
**Efficiency** of (A + B) = Total Work ÷ Days = 6 ÷ 3 = 2 units/day.

**Efficiency** of B = Total Work ÷ Days = 6 ÷ 6 = 1 unit/day.

**Efficiency** of A = (A + B) − B = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/day.

**Double work** = 6 × 2 = 12 units.

**Time** for A = 12 ÷ 1 = 12 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B) = 3 days

Time taken by B = 6 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of time taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 A + B 3 6 2
 B 6 1
**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of A = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Work to be done = **Double** of original work = 2 × 6 = 12 units

⇒ Time taken by A = Double Work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time taken by A = 12 ÷ 1 = 12 days

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Combined Efficiency Rule

The efficiency of two people working together is the sum of their individual efficiencies: EA₊B = EA + EB.

Work-Time Relationship

Time is inversely proportional to efficiency for a constant amount of work. If work is doubled, time taken at the same efficiency also doubles.</p

questions.question: Raman's income is ₹10,200. He saves 30% of his income. If his income increases by 14% and expenditure increases by 40%, then his savings will:

questions.question: A typist takes 40 minutes to type 2 pages. How many pages will he type in 80 minutes?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Time** taken is doubled from 40 minutes to 80 minutes.

Since the **typing rate** is constant, the **number of pages** will also double.

Number of pages = 2 × 2 = 4 pages.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 pages.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time₁ (T₁) = 40 minutes, Work₁ (W₁) = 2 pages

Time₂ (T₂) = 80 minutes, Work₂ (W₂) = ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5117b27309773c978a80ea835797a70e78aff478f7af035e20346e3db2a8dcf7.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Work is directly proportional to Time: (W₁ / T₁) = (W₂ / T₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 / 40 = W₂ / 80

⇒ W₂ = (2 × 80) ÷ 40

⇒ W₂ = 160 ÷ 40

⇒ W₂ = 4 pages

**∴ The correct answer is 4 pages.**

**__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

When efficiency is constant, the **work done** is directly proportional to the **time spent** (W ∝ T).

Unitary Method

Find the value of a **single unit** (pages per minute) first: 2 ÷ 40 = 0.05 pages/min, then multiply by the required time: 0.05 × 80 = 4 pages.

Work and Efficiency

The general formula is **Work = Efficiency × Time**. If Efficiency is same, W₁/T₁ = W₂/T₂.</p

questions.question: A jeep travels 80 km at the speed of 40 km/hr and the next 36 km at the speed of 18 km/hr. What is its average speed (in km/hr)?

__Shortcut Trick__

**Total Distance** = 80 + 36 = 116 km.

**Total Time** = (80 ÷ 40) + (36 ÷ 18) = 2 + 2 = 4 hours.

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 116 ÷ 4 = 29 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 29 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ef39f8ec40a1a7ca1a981c7fff689df5d2dc6f1d1744cf808b734e488f6c7c62.png] 

**Given:**

Distance 1 (D₁) = 80 km, Speed 1 (S₁) = 40 km/hr

Distance 2 (D₂) = 36 km, Speed 2 (S₂) = 18 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken for first part (T₁) = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 hours

⇒ Time taken for second part (T₂) = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 80 + 36 = 116 km

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 2 = 4 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 116 ÷ 4 = 29 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 29 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

If a body covers two equal distances at speeds **x** and **y**, the average speed is given by (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the difference of their speeds. In **opposite directions**, it is the sum of their speeds.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

**Pink : Red** = 17 × 15 : 2 × 15 = 255 : 30

• In **2025**, **Maharaja Sayajirao University (MSU) Vadodara** showcased major advancements in **3D bioprinting**, specifically focusing on its transformative role in **regenerative medicine and tissue engineering**.
 
• The demonstration highlighted the ability to create **complex biological structures** by utilizing **living cells** and specialized **bio-inks**, which are deposited **layer-by-layer** to form functional tissues.
 
• This technology at **MSU Vadodara** aims to address critical healthcare challenges by developing **lab-grown tissues** such as **skin grafts**, **bone scaffolds**, and **vascular networks**.
 
• The application in **regenerative medicine** focuses on the **repair** and **replacement** of damaged organs or tissues, potentially eliminating the need for traditional **organ donors** in the future.
 
• The **2025** demonstration emphasized **precision medicine**, where **3D bioprinting** is used to create patient-specific models for **surgical planning** and **drug efficacy testing**.

• **3D Bioprinting**: This is an **additive manufacturing** process that uses **biological materials** to fabricate structures that imitate the characteristics of **natural tissues**. It differs from standard 3D printing by using **living cells** instead of plastic or metal.
 
• **Bio-inks**: These are the "inks" used in bioprinters, typically composed of **hydrogels**, **growth factors**, and **nutrients** that sustain **cell viability** and promote **proliferation** during and after the printing process.
 
• **Tissue Engineering**: This is a scientific field that combines **engineering** and **life sciences** to develop **biological substitutes**. It often uses a **scaffold** to provide a **three-dimensional** framework for cells to attach and grow.
 
• **Regenerative Medicine**: This branch of medicine seeks to **regenerate** human cells, tissues, or organs to restore **normal function**. It includes **stem cell therapy** and **bio-fabrication** as core components.
 
• **Future Applications**: Beyond tissue repair, **3D bioprinting** is expected to revolutionize **pharmaceutical research** by allowing scientists to test new **drugs** on **printed human tissues**, significantly reducing the necessity for **animal testing** and improving the accuracy of **clinical trials**.

• **Biocompatibility**: The materials used at institutions like **MSU Vadodara** are selected for their **biocompatibility**, ensuring that the printed tissues do not trigger an **immune rejection** when integrated with natural biological systems.
 
• **Economic Impact**: By localizing the production of **bio-printed tissues** and **scaffolds** in **India**, the technology helps in making **advanced healthcare** more **affordable** and accessible.
</ul

questions.question: As announced in 2025, the headquarters of the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) will be established in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Cabinet**, chaired by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, approved the establishment of the **International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA)** with its permanent headquarters located in **India**.
 
• The **IBCA** was formally launched by the **Prime Minister** on **April 9, 2023**, during the **50th-anniversary** celebrations of **Project Tiger** held in **Mysuru**, **Karnataka**.
 
• The **Government of India** has committed a one-time budgetary support of **Rs. 150 crore** for a period of **five years**, spanning from **2023-24** to **2027-28**.
 
• The primary objective of the alliance is to ensure the long-term conservation of **seven major big cat species** across the globe by creating a common platform for **96 big cat range countries**.
 
• This initiative positions **India** as a global leader in wildlife conservation, as it is the only country in the world to have the **Tiger**, **Lion**, **Leopard**, **Snow Leopard**, and **Cheetah** (reintroduced) in its natural habitats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Seven Big Cats:**
 
 
• The alliance focuses on the conservation of the **Tiger**, **Lion**, **Leopard**, **Snow Leopard**, **Puma**, **Jaguar**, and **Cheetah**.
 
• Out of these seven species, **five** are currently found in **India**, making the country a critical stakeholder in global feline conservation.
 
 
 
• **Governance Structure:**
 
 
• The **IBCA** follows a governance model that includes a **General Assembly**, a **Council**, and a **Secretariat** (which is headquartered in **India**).
 
• The **Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change** of India plays a pivotal role in the initial administrative setup of the alliance.
 
 
 
• **Membership and Participation:**
 
 
• Membership is open to **96 range countries** that host these big cats, as well as non-range countries, **international organizations**, and scientific bodies interested in conservation.
 
• It aims to facilitate **knowledge sharing**, **capacity building**, and **resource mobilization** to mitigate human-wildlife conflict and illegal wildlife trade.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Strategies:**
 
 
• The alliance works on **benchmarking** conservation practices, **eco-tourism** development, and financial support for habitat restoration.
 
• It integrates **scientific research** with **traditional knowledge** to ensure sustainable populations of big cats in their respective **ecosystems**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Significance:** The establishment of **IBCA** is compared to the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)**, showcasing **India's** intent to lead multilateral environmental frameworks.
 
• **Project Tiger Legacy:** The launch coincided with **50 years** of the **Project Tiger** initiative (started in **1973**), which has been hailed as one of the most successful species conservation programs in the world.
 
• **Financial Framework:** After the initial **five-year** grant from **India**, the **IBCA** intends to sustain itself through **membership fees**, contributions from **multilateral institutions**, and **private sector** support.
 
• **Geographical Focus:** While **India** is the headquarters, the alliance focuses heavily on regions like **Africa**, **South America**, and **Central Asia** where species like the **Jaguar** and **Snow Leopard** face significant threats.
</ul

questions.question: In July 2025, which international city was in the spotlight for hosting the 17th BRICS Summit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rio de Janeiro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **17th BRICS Summit** is scheduled to be held in **2025** under the presidency of **Brazil**.
 
• **Rio de Janeiro**, one of the most prominent cities in **Brazil**, has been designated as the host city for this major international event in **July 2025**.
 
• The **BRICS** chairmanship follows a rotational system among the founding and primary members: **Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa**.
 
• Initially, **Brazil** was expected to host the **16th Summit** in **2024**, but due to logistical considerations and its **G20** presidency, the order was swapped with **Russia**, which hosted the **16th Summit** in **Kazan** in **October 2024**.
 
• The **2025** summit will be the first **BRICS** meeting in **Brazil** following the significant expansion of the bloc that took place in early **2024**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Rio de Janeiro.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of BRICS:**
 
 
• The group was originally conceived as **BRIC** (**Brazil, Russia, India, and China**) in **2006**.
 
• The first formal summit took place in **Yekaterinburg, Russia**, in **2009**.
 
• With the induction of **South Africa** in **2010**, the group was renamed **BRICS**.
 
 
 
• **2024 Expansion (BRICS+):**
 
 
• Effective **January 1, 2024**, the bloc expanded to include **Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE)**.
 
• This expansion reflects the group's goal of fostering a **multipolar world order** and increasing the influence of **Global South** economies.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance:**
 
 
• The **BRICS** nations combined represent approximately **45% of the world's population**.
 
• The group accounts for nearly **28% of the global economy** and a significant portion of the world's oil production and trade.
 
 
 
• **New Development Bank (NDB):**
 
 
• Established during the **6th BRICS Summit** in **Fortaleza, Brazil (2014)**, the **NDB** serves as an alternative to the **World Bank** and **IMF** for infrastructure and sustainable development projects.
 
• It is headquartered in **Shanghai, China**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Host City Profile:** **Rio de Janeiro** is a coastal city in **Brazil** known for its **Copacabana** and **Ipanema** beaches, and it has a long history of hosting major global events, including the **2016 Summer Olympics** and the **2024 G20 Summit**.
 
• **Summit Objectives:** The **17th Summit** is expected to focus on **strengthening multilateralism**, **sustainable energy transitions**, and **reforming international financial institutions** to better represent emerging markets.
 
• **Member Roles:** **Brazil's** leadership in **2025** is seen as a pivotal moment for the country to reassert its influence in **global diplomacy** and economic cooperation within the **Atlantic** and **South American** regions.
</ul

questions.question: Dassault Aviation and Reliance Aerostructure Limited (RAL), in June 2025, announced at Paris Air Show execution of an agreement to manufacture which of the following in India for the Global Market by 2028?

The correct answer is __**Falcon 2000 LXS Business Executive Jets**__.

__
 
• **Dassault Aviation** and **Reliance Aerostructure Limited (RAL)**, through their joint venture **Dassault Reliance Aerospace Limited (DRAL)**, announced a significant expansion of their partnership in **June 2025** during the **Paris Air Show**.
 
• The agreement outlines the execution of a plan to manufacture the **Falcon 2000 LXS Business Executive Jets** entirely in **India**, intended for the **Global Market**.
 
• The manufacturing process is slated to reach full scale with the first completed aircraft expected to be ready by the year **2028**.
 
• The production facility is located at the **Dhirubhai Ambani Aerospace Park (DAAP)** in the **Mihan SEZ** of **Nagpur, Maharashtra**.
 
• This move marks a transition from manufacturing components and sub-assemblies to the **Final Assembly Line (FAL)** for a complete business jet in **India**, supporting the **Make in India** initiative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Dassault Aviation:** It is a premier **French** aerospace company that designs and builds military aircraft, such as the **Rafale** and **Mirage**, and the **Falcon** family of business jets. The company has a long-standing relationship with **India** dating back to the **1950s**.
 
• **Dassault Reliance Aerospace Limited (DRAL):** This is a **Joint Venture** established in **2017**, where **Reliance Aerostructure Limited** holds a **51%** stake and **Dassault Aviation** holds **49%**. It was initially formed to help fulfill **offset obligations** related to the **36 Rafale jet deal**.
 
• **Falcon 2000 LXS:** This specific model is a twin-engine **business jet** known for its efficiency and capability to land on **short runways**. It offers a range of approximately **4,000 nautical miles** (7,410 km) and can carry up to **10 passengers** in a widebody cabin configuration.
 
• **Strategic Significance:** By establishing a **Final Assembly Line** in **Nagpur**, the project enhances **India's** aerospace ecosystem, promotes **high-skill employment**, and positions the country as a competitive exporter in the **civil aviation** sector.
 
• **Historical Context:** Previously, the **Nagpur** facility was involved in producing **cockpit front sections** and **fuel tanks** for the **Falcon** jets. The **2025** agreement represents the ultimate scale-up to full aircraft integration and flight testing within **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Paris Air Show:** Held at **Le Bourget**, it is one of the world's oldest and largest aerospace exhibitions, often serving as a venue for major **international defense** and **civilian aviation** contracts.
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat:** This project is a cornerstone for **self-reliance** in the **aerospace and defense** sectors, reducing dependency on imported finished aircraft and boosting **indigenous manufacturing** capabilities.
 
• **Technological Transfer:** The agreement involves a high degree of **technology transfer** from **France** to **India**, ensuring that **Indian** engineers and technicians are trained in world-class **aerospace assembly** standards.
</ul

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India revised Priority Sector Lending (PSL) guidelines for Small Finance Banks from FY 2025–26, reducing the PSL target to what percentage of ANBC (adjusted net bank credit) or Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposures (CEOBE)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**60%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, in a notification issued in **April 2024**, announced a significant revision to the **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)** targets for **Small Finance Banks (SFBs)** to bring them on par with universal banks.
 
• As per the revised guidelines, the overall **PSL target** for **Small Finance Banks**, which was previously mandated at **75%**, will be reduced in a phased manner. For the financial year **2025–26** (specifically by **March 31, 2026**), the target has been set at **60%** of **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** or **Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE)**, whichever is higher.
 
• The primary objective of this revision is to provide a **level playing field** for **SFBs** and to harmonize their regulatory requirements with those of **Universal Banks**, which currently have a **40%** PSL target.
 
• Before this revision, **Small Finance Banks** were required to maintain a much higher threshold of **75%** to ensure that credit reached the **unserved and underserved sections** of the population, including small farmers and micro-units.
 
• The **RBI** has implemented a **glide path** for this transition: the target remains **75%** until **March 31, 2025**; it reduces to **60%** by **March 31, 2026**; and finally reaches **40%** by **March 31, 2027**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Priority Sector Lending (PSL):** It is a **regulatory framework** established by the **RBI** that mandates banks to allocate a specific portion of their **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** to certain sectors that are considered vital for the **inclusive development** of the country. These sectors include **Agriculture**, **Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)**, **Export Credit**, **Education**, **Housing**, **Social Infrastructure**, and **Renewable Energy**.
 
• **Small Finance Banks (SFBs):** These are a specific category of banks established to provide **financial inclusion** to sections of the economy not being served by other banks. They are registered as **public limited companies** under the **Companies Act, 2013** and are governed by the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**. Notable examples include **AU Small Finance Bank**, **Equitas Small Finance Bank**, and **Jana Small Finance Bank**.
 
• **ANBC and CEOBE:** **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** represents the total credit provided by a bank after making specific adjustments for bills rediscounted and other prescribed exemptions. **Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE)** refers to the potential credit risk from non-fund-based limits like **letters of credit** or **bank guarantees**.
 
• **Regulatory Scope:** While the overall target is being reduced, **SFBs** are still required to focus on their core mission of serving **Small and Marginal Farmers** and **Weaker Sections**. The **RBI** maintains specific sub-targets within the PSL framework to ensure these vulnerable groups continue to receive adequate credit flow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility for SFBs:** To be eligible for a license, the **minimum paid-up voting equity capital** for **SFBs** was initially **Rs. 100 crore**, which has been increased to **Rs. 200 crore** in recent guidelines, except for those transitioned from **Urban Co-operative Banks**.
 
• **The Glide Path Schedule:**
 
 
• **75%**: Applicable up to the end of **FY 2024-25**.
 
• **60%**: Target for the end of **FY 2025-26**.
 
• **40%**: Final target to be achieved by the end of **FY 2026-27**.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Revision:** This move is expected to improve the **profitability** and **operational flexibility** of **Small Finance Banks**, as they can now diversify their loan portfolios toward higher-yielding non-priority sectors as they grow in size and scale.
 
• **Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks (UCBs):** It is important to note that **UCBs** are also on a similar glide path to reach a **75%** PSL target by **March 31, 2026**, showing the **RBI's** efforts to balance different banking tiers according to their specific mandates and risks.
